key_insight: Neural topology optimization with KATO can design ship structures that cut vibration-driven active input power while staying connected and manufacturable.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets propulsion-induced vibrations in decks and foundations, helping reduce noise, fatigue, and equipment damage in ship structures.
method: Uses a convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KATO) to reparameterize topology optimization.
Optimizes active input power (AIP) under forced vibration, with Helmholtz filtering and Heaviside projection for feature-size control.
Compares against GCMMA and evaluates static compliance, resonance behavior, and manufacturability-aware/stress-aware variants.
evidence_signal: Across deck and frame cases, KATO matched or improved AIP versus references and GCMMA, with up to 32 dB AIP reduction near resonance, 22–36x lower binary static compliance, and 6.4–10.4x faster runtimes in stress-aware formulations.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on the chosen frequency cases, filter/projection settings, and post-processing steps such as finite-depth extrusion and matched-volume binary re-analysis.
paper_title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
